newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks storm to record high at open.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks storm to record high at open.

text.p: The Australian share market stormed to a record high at the open on Wednesday with traders taking their cue from U.S. markets that surged after economic data calmed inflation fears.
The All Ordinaries index leapt 30.7 points to 2,509.8, surpassing the previous record high of 2,508.3 reached on February 19, 1997.
Rises were across the board, with all the leaders showing handsome gains early on.

Bellwether BHP lived up to its leading role, jumping nearly three percent to an intraday high of A$18.40 (US$14.35) before easing back slightly, as investors continued to buy in after Tuesday's steel restructuring announcement.
"BHP has probably been the standout on the back of its proposed restructuring," said broker Tony Russell of Morgan Stockbroking.

Sydney Harbour Casino went against the trend, losing six cents to A$2.12 on newspaper reports that would-be manager, Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd, could withdraw from its offer to buy management control of the casino.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of nearly five to one, while about 38 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
